Deneysville Drowning in Sewage

By: Anna-Maria van Niekerk | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
The sewage spills around Deneysville on the Vaal Dam are worse than ever. Two years of exposes and pressure seem to no avail. What now?

Unique Selling Point:
Two years ago we broke the story of how Deneysville's sewage treatment plant was over-capacity and how raw sewage was flooding into the Vaal Dam. For months the residents kept on sending us a steady supply of damning photographs and videos of how the problem was being ignored.

We returned with promises from the then Director-General and signs of hope when the ANC was voted out of office and a DA-coalition took over after municipal elections last year.

Now we return to find the situation even more dire -- with the DA councillor living in the area having laid criminal charges against the Municipal Manager and absolutely no progress on the investigation and local sewage sleuth Peet Schabort still investigating the degrading, dehumanising conditions where people have to live in the filth.

Press Release:


Report Card: Deneysville Drowns in Sewage
In a brand new regular segment called Report Card, Carte Blanche returns to previous stories to find out what improvements or changes have been made and to hold those
officials in charge personally accountable. This week following three exposés over two years, we head back to Deneysville along the Vaal Dam to investigate whether
sewage spills are a thing of the past or worse than ever. Deneysville's sewage treatment plant was operating way beyond its capacity flooding the Vaal Dam with raw
sewage. For months residents kept sending us a steady supply of photographs and videos. Who will score an F on their report card and fail dismally or perhaps get the
thumbs up?


Script:


INSERT SCRIPT:
JUNE 2015: In June 2015 the holiday village Deneysville and township Refengkgotso on the Free State side of the Vaal Dam became the poster child for everything that’s wrong with municipalities crippled by failing infrastructure and incapacity to fix their people’s problems.
DEREK LINK: This treatment plant – clearly unable to deal with the amount of sewage it’s meant to process is just half the problem – a disturbing and unhealthy amount of sewage isn’t even reaching this plant.
Sewage flooded the cemetery, in between houses and across farmland into the Vaal Dam. Dangerous trenches had been dug to stem the flow – the system designed for 4000 people was serving over 20,000. Outrage spiked when the Metsimaholo municipality lay a new pipeline to take treated effluent from the plant to the Vaal Dam.
ANDRE JOHNSON: Nobody was informed. Nobody was consulted. Nothing.
PEET SCHABORT: Another thing with this pipeline – as quickly as they lay it, they covered it.
Metsimaholo spokesman Gino Alberts admitted they’d proceeded in error and should have applied for a water use licence – that would have required public consultation.
DR GINO ALBERTS: It was an oversight from our side. We thought that the operating licence that we have is sufficient.
DEREK LINK: That was the situation in Refengkgotso two years ago and after many plans and promises from the Metsimaholo Municipality we’ve come to check on the situation now and give them a score card.
TITLE: REPORT CARD – METSIMAHOLO MUNICIPALITY
Retiree turned activist Peet Schabort tracks problems.
PEET SCHABORT: Pleased to see you people again.
DEREK WATTS: I see the pump’s working, hey?
PEET SCHABORT: Yes. The pump is working. The one auger. The other one is not working for many years.
DEREK WATTS: This pump station on our report card we’d can say that it has improved?
PEET SCHABORT: Let’s say so, but it’s still unexplainable the amount of sewerage laying here.
DEREK WATTS: We’re going to give them a pass...we’re giving them 51%
PEET SCHABORT: Yes, we give them 51%.
REPORT CARD: PUMP STATION 1 = C
The second pump broke down about five months ago.
PEET SCHABORT: They get rid of the sewage by opening the manholes...and also some of these houses are standing in sewerage.
DEREK WATTS: So what are we giving it on the score card?
PEET SCHABORT: What is below junk status?
DEREK WATTS: Below junk status?
Vinolia Msibi’s family bears the brunt of this broken pump.
VINOLIA MSIBI: Sometimes you get sick because of this smell here. We can’t do something because of this smell. We have to eat, this smell is here. We can’t even open the door or the windows. Everything is bad here. We’ve been complaining, but nothing is really happening...
DEREK WATTS: So Vinolia out of a hundred what percent would you give the municipality here?
VINOLIA MSIBI: Ten.
DEREK: 10%
VINOLIA MSIBI: I’ll give them 10%.
REPORT CARD: PUMP STATION 2 - FF
In 2015 DA councilor Johan Geyser laid a charge of pollution against the Municipal Manager. It’s gone nowhere. By 2017 following the local government elections, the DA-led coalition had broken down.
JOHAN GEYSER: There’s actually nothing happening at the moment...the township is absolutely in a state, the people complain every day, they complain at me... try and fix it for a while and it’s fixed up for maybe a month or two and then it’s back to normal again. It starts all over again.
Thabang Mahlasela is fed up.
THABANG MAHLASELA: Yes, they are angry, it’s just that they can’t take the law into their own hands, and they respect the councillor. The councillors are not respecting the residents.
Hope flared when Director-General for Water and Sanitation Margaret-Ann Diedricks secured R142-million for Deneysville’s revamp.
MARGARET-ANN DIEDERICKS: I can certainly commit myself to joining you, to taking you on that roadshow, to show the progress without a doubt...
But Diedricks resigned just after approving the water use licence for the new pipe and strict conditions applied: the plant must be expanded to make the effluent safe.
From recent minutes of the Vaal Reservoir Forum meeting it appear that the project ground to halt after the DG left.
REPORT CARD: PLANT UPGRADE - E
Red flags persist in quality reports the final effluent that goes into the dam, near where RandWater draws its bulk supply.
REPORT CARD: EFFLUENT QUALITY - F
Spokesman Gino Alberts says they’re aware of the broken pump – he says it will be fixed when the plant is upgraded. Contractors have moved onto the site this month – they should take 24 months to finish upgrades.
DEREK LINK: According to the email from the municipality nothing has happened here at the treatment works for two years and they can’t cope with the effluent. So by their own admission it has to be a fail.
REPORT CARD: FAIL
PROMOS
10”
Two years after our first expose on the run-down, under-capacity sewage works in Deneysville on the Vaal Dam we return to give a report card on the state of affairs.

15”
Why has there been so little progress in upgrading Deneysville’s defunct sewage works?
VINOLIA MSIBI: We can’t do some things because of this smell. We have to eat, this smell is here. We can’t even open the door or the windows. Everything is bad here. We’ve been complaining, but nothing is really happening...

15”
It’s hope deferred in Deneysville on the Vaal Dam as upgrading of the sewage works is delayed.
DEREK WATTS: So what are we giving it on the score card?
PEET SCHABORT: What is below junk status?
DEREK WATTS: Below junk status?
FINAL SCORE:
Pump 1 – D 51
Pump 2 – FF 20
Plant upgrade – E 40
Effluent quality – F 30
AVERAGE: F 35%
